cutoff_window.policy: Only sources with a visible publication or material-update timestamp strictly after the start and no later than the run timestamp qualify. Date-only sources at a window boundary are excluded.

qualifying_findings.title: AtlasAiDev MCP Server for WordPress incorrect privilege assignment
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Public GitHub Advisory Database record, with the NVD record and Patchstack CNA advisory referenced by that record.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: AtlasAiDev MCP Server for WordPress (ai-workflow-automation-ai-agent-hub) through version 2.0.3. GitHub's record does not list a fixed version; the referenced Patchstack advisory should control remediation verification.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: CVE-2026-125771 / GHSA-w68m-3rvm-5xxq reports CWE-266 incorrect privilege assignment allowing privilege escalation in the WordPress MCP plugin through 2.0.3. The public advisory is rated High (CVSS 3.1 7.2) and was published to GitHub's Advisory Database at 15:30:41Z on November 15.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An MCP server acting on a WordPress installation bridges an AI client to administrative web actions. Incorrect privilege assignment can expand the authority available through that delegated tool boundary.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: The product's general catalog entry belongs in ai-wiki; this repository retains the MCP delegated-authority finding, affected range, and remediation-verification note.

qualifying_findings.title: vLLM common-prefix KV-cache race condition
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Public GitHub Advisory Database record with linked public vLLM fix commit and v0.32.0 release reference.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: vllm-project/vllm 0.30.0 and 0.31.0; the advisory identifies single_type_kv_cache_manager.py's Common Prefix Handler. It names v0.32.0 and commit e687a251bb056fa527846633f7a1b0a6c0f42374 as remediation.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: CVE-2026-129356 / GHSA-fj8v-85jv-jwpv describes a remotely reachable, high-complexity race condition in vLLM's Common Prefix Handler. The advisory says public exploit material exists and recommends upgrading to 0.32.0; it is rated Low (CVSS 3.1 5.0).
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: KV-cache and prefix sharing are inference-runtime isolation surfaces. A concurrency flaw in this component merits release-gate review where vLLM serves concurrent or mutually untrusted workloads, even though the public advisory assigns low severity and high attack complexity.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: vLLM product and runtime background are upstream-owned in ai-wiki; retain the security-specific inference-runtime race, affected releases, patch reference, and tenancy-isolation implication locally.

upstream_routing.local_retention: MCP delegated-authority privilege-escalation finding and remediation verification.
Inference-runtime cache race, affected versions, fix reference, and tenant-isolation relevance.

confidence_notes: High confidence that both findings were newly published in the window because the public GitHub Advisory Database API reports ISO-8601 timestamps inside it.

Medium confidence in the WordPress plugin's fixed version: the public GHSA identifies the affected range but leaves package/version data empty; verify the Patchstack CNA remediation before durable synthesis.

Medium confidence in exploitability characterization for CVE-2026-129356: the GHSA states that public exploit material exists and links the vLLM patch, but the reporter-authored advisory should be reconciled with vLLM maintainer release notes during synthesis.
follow_up_actions: Before synthesis, verify the MCP Server for WordPress fixed version and vendor remediation in the Patchstack CNA source; preserve the advisory's high-privilege-required CVSS condition.
Before synthesis, verify that vLLM 0.32.0 includes commit e687a251bb056fa527846633f7a1b0a6c0f42374 and assess whether deployments share Common Prefix Handler state across security principals.
Do not duplicate the previously ingested ContextForge identity-propagation finding merely because its public advisory metadata was later updated.
collection_blockers: No collection blocker. The local worktree contained pre-existing untracked .Codex/agent-claim and .agent-ops paths; they were not modified.
